scope: Theorem 5.2 (Weighted cohomology for residue currents) of the manuscript “Global Spherical Shells on Minimal Surfaces of Class VII” (preprints/Global-Spherical-Shells-on-Minimal-Surfaces-of-Class-VII-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 060 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d441e45f773bce9f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix ε > 0 and b > ε. Let F be either OY or an end-framed compact datum E with an integrable operator satisfying (4.3). Consider the current complex C2,q −ε,b,−3(F) = W−3−q −ε,b (Λ2,q ⊗ F), q = 0, 1, 2. (5.7) Its cohomology is finite-dimensional. For F = OY its degree-one cohomology is zero. In particular every closed scalar (2, 1)-current in this space which is zero on a positive tail is exact. If a degree-zero current β ∈ W−3 −ε,b(Λ2,0 ⊗ F) satisfies ¯ ∂F β = J for a degree-one current J supported in {h ≤ C}, then β vanishes on a positive tail. Finally, an order-zero (2, 1)-current supported in {h ≤ C} whose masses on negative unit height slabs are at most C0eµl belongs to this complex whenever b > µ. The same Sobolev order and pair of rates can be used for any family with that common exponent µ, regardless of its individual constants and upper support bounds.
